mainTopic: Acquiring ownerless land (נכסי הגר) through חזקה: which acts count, the role of the person's purpose in שמואל's rulings, and how far one act reaches.
overview: This amud is about how a person acquires ownerless land, such as the property of a גר who died without heirs, by doing a חזקה. First the גמרא finishes a ruling: throwing turnip seeds into cracks in the ground is not a חזקה, because the land improved later on its own and not at the moment of the act. Then שמואל gives four parallel rulings: trimming a palm tree, clearing wood, leveling bumps, and letting water into a field. Each act acquires the land only if it was done to improve the land, and not for some other use like animal feed, firewood, a threshing floor, or catching fish. For each case the גמרא asks היכי דמי and shows how the way the work was done reveals the person's purpose. A story about a woman who cut palm branches for thirteen years, but lost the tree to a man who hoed a little beneath it, teaches that taking benefit is not a real act of possession. רב then rules that drawing a picture on a גר's property acquires it, and he proves this from his own garden. The amud ends with an argument between רב and שמואל about whether one hoe-strike in a field with clear borders acquires the whole field or only the spot that was struck. That discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Throwing turnip seeds into cracks is not a valid acquisition
steps.stepSummary: Someone who threw turnip seeds into the cracks of a dead convert's field does not acquire it by חזקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone threw turnip seeds into the cracks of the ground of a convert's field, that does not count as a חזקה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a ruling: tossing turnip seeds into the cracks of an ownerless field does not acquire it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Land of a גר who died without heirs is ownerless, and anyone can acquire it by doing an act of improvement (חזקה). Throwing seeds into cracks might seem like planting, but the ruling says it does not count. The reason comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Cracks or crevices in the ground
A convert; if he dies with no Jewish heirs, his property becomes ownerless
An act of ownership that acquires land

phrases.english: who threw turnip seeds
into the cracks of the land of a convert
it is not a valid act of acquisition.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּשְׁדָא לִיפְתָּא בֵּי פִילֵי דְּאַרְעָא דְגֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a ruling begun before this section
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Throwing seeds into cracks of ownerless land is not a חזקה.

steps.title: Why the seed-throwing does not count
steps.stepSummary: When he threw the seeds, the land was not improved. The later improvement happened by itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? At the moment he threw the seeds, the land was not improved. Now that it is improved, it improved on its own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks מאי טעמא and explains the ruling from the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חזקה must improve the land at the moment it is done. The throwing itself added nothing. The later growth came by itself, through nature, not through a human act, so it cannot count as his act of acquisition.
steps.whatToRemember: A חזקה requires an improvement at the time of the act itself, not one that happens later on its own.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
At the time that he threw them
there was no improvement;
now that it is improved
it improved by itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason for the ruling in step 1
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why throwing seeds is not a חזקה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: There was no improvement at the time of the act; the later improvement happened on its own.

steps.title: Trimming a palm tree: it depends on the purpose
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that cutting branches off a palm tree acquires it only if done for the tree's benefit, not to get animal feed.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: Someone who trims a palm tree acquires it if he did it for the tree, but does not acquire it if he did it for his animals.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives the first of four parallel rulings: the same physical act can acquire or fail to acquire, depending on its purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Trimming helps the tree grow, so it counts as improving the property. If he was really only collecting branches to feed his animals, he was taking for himself, not improving the land, so he does not acquire it.

keyTerms.meaning: With the intention of, for the purpose of

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
One who cuts branches off a palm tree:
if it is for the sake of the palm tree, he acquires it;
if it is for the sake of the animals, he does not acquire it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הַאי מַאן דְּפָשַׁח דִּיקְלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New ruling in the same topic of acquiring by חזקה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Trimming a palm acquires it only if done for the tree's benefit.

steps.title: How we know why he trimmed the palm
steps.stepSummary: Cutting from both sides shows he was helping the tree. Cutting all from one side shows he wanted feed.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? If he took branches from this side and that side, it was for the tree. If he took all of them from one side, it was for the animals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks היכי דמי, meaning how we can tell his intention, and answers from the way he cut.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We cannot read his mind, so the method of cutting reveals his purpose. Balanced trimming on both sides helps the tree grow. Stripping one side is just harvesting branches.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How is it pictured?

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
If he took from this side and from that side,
it was for the sake of the palm tree.
If all of it was from one side,
it was for the sake of the animals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines how to identify the intention in step 3
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How we can tell his intention
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Two-sided cutting means for the tree; one-sided cutting means for the animals.

steps.title: Clearing wood from a field: it depends on the purpose
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that clearing trees and wood acquires the field only if done to improve the land, not to gather firewood.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל also said: Someone who clears a field acquires it if he did it for the land, but does not acquire it if he did it to collect wood.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a second ruling built on the same pattern as the palm tree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Clearing the field gets it ready for plowing, and that is an improvement. Gathering wood for himself does not improve anything, so it is not a חזקה.

keyTerms.meaning: Clears a field (of trees or wood)

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
One who clears a field:
if it is for the sake of the land, he acquires it;
if it is for the sake of the wood, he does not acquire it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הַאי מַאן דְּזָכֵי זִיכְיָא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Clearing a field acquires it only if done for the land.

steps.title: How we know why he cleared the wood
steps.stepSummary: Taking both big and small pieces shows he was clearing the land. Leaving the small pieces shows he only wanted wood.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? If he took big and small pieces, it was for the land. If he took the big pieces and left the small ones, it was for the wood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא again asks היכי דמי and shows how his method reveals his intention.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone preparing the land removes everything, even the small pieces. Someone collecting firewood takes only the useful big pieces and leaves the rest.

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
If he took big and small pieces,
it was for the sake of the land;
if he took big pieces and left the small ones,
it was for the sake of the wood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines how to identify the intention in step 5
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How we can tell his intention
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Taking everything means for the land; taking only the big pieces means for the wood.

steps.title: Leveling the ground: it depends on the purpose
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that leveling bumps acquires the field only if done to improve it for farming, not to make a threshing floor.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל also said: Someone who levels bumps in the ground acquires it if he did it for the land, but does not acquire it if he did it to make a threshing floor.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives the third ruling in the same pattern.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leveling the whole field for plowing improves the land. Flattening areas only to make a threshing floor serves his own use, not the field's improvement, so it is not a חזקה.

keyTerms.meaning: A bump or uneven spot in the ground

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
One who levels out bumps in the ground:
if it is for the sake of the land, he acquires it;
if it is for the sake of a threshing floor, he does not acquire it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הַאי מַאן דְּאתָקֵיל תִּיקְלָא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Leveling acquires the field only if done for the land.

steps.title: How we know why he leveled the ground
steps.stepSummary: Moving a mound into a ditch shows he was improving the field. Flattening mounds and ditches each in place shows he wanted a threshing floor.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? If he took a mound and threw it into a ditch, it was for the land. If he flattened mound into mound and ditch into ditch, it was for a threshing floor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks היכי דמי again and gives the sign that reveals his intention.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Filling the ditch with dirt from the mound evens out the whole field for farming. Leveling each spot separately just makes a flat working surface and leaves the field uneven.
steps.whatToRemember: In each of these rulings of שמואל, the same act counts as a חזקה only if it improves the land. The way the work is done shows what the person intended.

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
If he took a mound and threw it into a ditch,
it was for the sake of the land.
If it was a mound within a mound and a ditch within a ditch,
phrases.notes: He flattened each spot where it was, without moving dirt from the high spots to the low spots.

phrases.english: it was for the sake of a threshing floor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines how to identify the intention in step 7
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How we can tell his intention
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Moving a mound into a ditch means for the land; leveling each spot in place means for a threshing floor.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A חזקה works only when the act truly improves the land, and the method of the work shows the purpose.

steps.title: Letting water into a field: for the land or for the fish
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that opening a water channel into ownerless land acquires it only if it was done to water the land, not to catch fish.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: if someone opens a way for water to flow into a piece of land, and he did it for the land, he acquires it. If he did it to catch fish, he does not acquire it.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives another rule in the same pattern as before: an act on the land acquires it only if it was done to improve the land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same idea as the cases of cutting trees and leveling bumps. Letting water in can help the field by watering it. It can also just be a way to catch fish. Only the first kind of act is a real חזקה.

keyTerms.meaning: opened a way for water to flow in

phrases.english: And שמואל said:
This one who opened water into land:
if he did it for the land, he acquires it;
if he did it for the fish, he does not acquire it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הַאי מַאן דְּפָתַח מַיָּא בְּאַרְעָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fourth rule by שמואל in the same series about why an act was done.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Letting water into land acquires it only when done to water the land, not to catch fish.

steps.title: How can we tell which purpose he had?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we can know whether he let the water in for the land or for the fish.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? How do we tell?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question that sets up the next step: how can a court see what he had in mind?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A court cannot read minds. So the rule only works if there is a sign we can see that shows his purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the case? how does it look in practice?

phrases.english: What is the case?
phrases.notes: He is asking how we can know from the outside what the person meant to do.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a visible sign behind שמואל's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A visible sign that shows whether the water was let in for the land or for fish.

steps.title: Two gates means fish, one gate means land
steps.stepSummary: Opening one gate in and one gate out shows he wanted fish. Opening only one gate shows he wanted to water the land.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he opened two gates, one to let water in and one to let it out, he did it for the fish. If he opened one gate, he did it for the land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by giving a clear sign of what he had in mind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Water flowing in and then out carries fish through, where he can catch them, so that shows a fishing plan. With one gate, the water stays and soaks the field, which shows he wanted to help the land.
steps.whatToRemember: In all of שמואל's cases, the same act can acquire land or not, depending on whether it was done to improve the land. We judge his purpose by a sign we can see.

phrases.english: If he opened two gates,
one bringing water in and one taking it out,
he did it for the fish.
If he opened one gate, he did it for the land.

steps.triggerLanguage: פָּתַח תְּרֵי בָבֵי, חַד מְעַיֵּיל וְחַד מַפֵּיק
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Two gates (in and out) show he wanted fish. One gate shows he wanted to water the land.

steps.title: The woman with the palm tree and the man who hoed under it
steps.stepSummary: A woman cut branches from an ownerless palm tree for thirteen years. A man then hoed a little under it, and the judge gave the tree to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman used a palm tree for thirteen years by cutting its branches. Then a man came and hoed a little under it. The case came before לוי, and some say before מר עוקבא, and he gave the tree to the man.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real court case about who acquires ownerless property. It sets up the woman's complaint, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The woman used the tree for a long time, but only by taking from it. The man did a small act, but it was work on the land. The ruling shows that taking benefit from the land is not a חזקה, while work on the land is.

keyTerms.meaning: left it in his hands, ruled it was his

phrases.english: There was a certain woman who ate from a palm tree
phrases.notes: Here 'ate' means she got benefit from the tree.

phrases.english: by cutting its branches, for thirteen years.
A certain man came
phrases.notes: Some versions add the word in square brackets, 'man'; others leave it out.

phrases.english: and hoed under it a little.
The case came before לוי,
and some say before מר עוקבא,
and he left it in his hands.
phrases.notes: In the man's hands. The man who hoed got the tree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A real case that applies the idea that only acts that improve the land count as a חזקה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hoing the land acquires it. Years of cutting branches does not.

steps.title: The woman protests the ruling
steps.stepSummary: The woman comes and cries out to the judge that the ruling is unfair.
steps.simpleTranslation: She came and cried out before him.
steps.whatsHappening: The woman complains that the ruling is unfair. This sets up the judge's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her complaint is the natural one: thirteen years of use should beat a little hoeing. This is the challenge the judge must answer.

phrases.english: She came crying out before him.

steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that gave the tree to the man who hoed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: She used the tree for thirteen years, so how can a little hoeing take it from her?

steps.title: You did not take possession the way people do
steps.stepSummary: The judge answers that her cutting of branches was not a real act of possession.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to her: What can I do for you? You did not take possession the way people take possession.
steps.whatsHappening: The judge explains why she lost: what she did was not a real חזקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: How long she used the tree does not matter. What matters is the kind of act. Taking branches is only taking benefit, while hoeing is work on the land the way owners normally take hold of property.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a חזקה of three years of use, which proves a claim of ownership. Here the question is how to acquire ownerless property, and for that you need an act of work on the land.
steps.whatToRemember: To acquire ownerless land, you must do a real act of work on the land itself. Just taking benefit from it, even for many years, is not enough.

phrases.english: He said to her: What can I do for you,
since you did not take possession the way people take possession.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines what counts as a real act of possession
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Long use of the tree should give her ownership.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a normal act of possession, like work on the land, acquires it. Taking benefit does not.

steps.title: Drawing a picture on a convert's property acquires it
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that drawing a picture on the property of a convert who left no heirs acquires it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: One who draws a picture on the property of a convert acquires it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב adds a new kind of act that acquires ownerless property: drawing a picture on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Drawing a picture, like painting on a wall, improves the property and makes it look nicer. That is enough to count as a חזקה, even though it is not farm work.

keyTerms.meaning: property of a convert (who died without heirs, so no one owns it)

phrases.english: רב said:
One who draws a picture on the property of a convert acquires it,
phrases.notes: This means a convert who died without heirs, so his property belongs to no one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: הַצָּר צוּרָה בְּנִכְסֵי הַגֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new example of an act that acquires ownerless property.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Drawing a picture on ownerless property acquires it.

steps.title: רב acquired his own garden this way
steps.stepSummary: Support for the rule: רב himself acquired the garden of the בית רב only by drawing a picture.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רב acquired the garden of the בית רב only by drawing a picture.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רב's rule by pointing to what רב himself did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב trusted this act enough to use it for his own property. So it is clear that he held drawing a picture to be a full חזקה.

keyTerms.meaning: the garden of the study house of רב

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַב לָא קָנֵי לְגִנְּתָא דְּבֵי רַב,
phrases.english: for רב acquired the garden of the בית רב
only by drawing a picture.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַב לָא קָנֵי לְגִנְּתָא דְּבֵי רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב's rule from his own actions.
steps.raayaObject: רב's ruling that drawing a picture acquires ownerless property.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב acquired the garden of the בית רב by drawing a picture.

steps.title: One hoe-strike in a field with clear borders
steps.stepSummary: רב says one hoe-strike in a field with clear borders acquires the whole field. שמואל says it acquires only the spot that was struck.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: a field with clear borders. רב הונא said in the name of רב: once he strikes it with a hoe one time, he acquires all of it. שמואל said: he acquires only the spot where he struck.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new argument between רב and שמואל about how much land one small act acquires.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree that one hoe-strike is a real חזקה. They argue about how far it reaches. רב holds that clear borders make the field one unit, so all of it is acquired. שמואל holds that the act only covers the exact spot where it was done.
steps.whyThisMatters: This argument sets up the next discussion: how much of a property one act of חזקה acquires.

phrases.english: It was stated: a field that is marked off by its borders:
רב הונא said that רב said:
once he struck it with one hoe-strike,
he acquired all of it.
And שמואל said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא קָנָה אֶלָּא מְקוֹם מַכּוֹשׁוֹ בִּלְבַד.
phrases.english: He acquired only the spot of his hoe-strike.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: how much land one act of חזקה covers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: one hoe-strike in a field with clear borders acquires the whole field. שמואל: only the spot that was struck.
